items.question: If RAG retrieved a passage, can the answer claim be considered grounded?
items.answer: Not automatically. Check that the passage is relevant, complete, current, permitted, and actually supports the claim. The model can misread evidence or answer beyond it, so retrieval and answer groundedness need separate evaluation.
items.trap: Retrieval presence is not entailment. A nearby or partial passage can be insufficient or even misleading.

items.question: Would fine-tuning be the right fix for a product that must answer from frequently changing private records?
items.answer: Usually not by itself. Use retrieval for changing, private, source-attributed facts, with access control and provenance. Fine-tuning is more suited to stable behavior or style when suitable training data exists; first measure the failure and baseline.
items.trap: Fine-tuning changes learned behavior; it is not a live, permission-aware database and does not replace current retrieval or authorization.

items.question: Why do teams over-build vector search first?
items.answer: It is the default pattern taught in tutorials, even when the questions are structured queries.
items.trap: Because vector databases are cheaper than SQL.

items.question: What answer signals vocabulary without judgement?
items.answer: Listing RAG components instead of naming cases where retrieval is the wrong tool.
items.trap: Saying RAG is always better than fine-tuning.

mcqs.question: Which observation most strongly indicates a RAG retrieval problem rather than a generation problem?
options: The required passage was not retrieved
The passage was retrieved and the answer paraphrased it correctly
The model used the cited passage and stated its limitation
The answer was formatted as JSON
mcqs.explanation: If the required permitted evidence never reaches context, investigate parsing, indexing, query, ranking, or filters. If it is present, generation faithfulness becomes the next question; JSON formatting is unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which failure is a chunking problem?
options: The model temperature is too high
Answers cut across chunk boundaries so no chunk holds the complete fact
mcqs.explanation: Bad chunking splits facts; adjusting size and overlap is the first fix to try.

mcqs.question: Which pipeline step handles PDFs, HTML and images for retrieval?
options: Fine-tuning the model on the documents
Converting sources into clean text chunks the model can read and the index can store
mcqs.explanation: Document processing is part of grounding: what the model reads must be extracted and normalised first.

mcqs.question: What does hybrid retrieval combine?
options: Keyword and vector search, usually fused and then re-ranked
mcqs.explanation: Hybrid search covers exact terms and semantic similarity, and re-ranking sharpens ordering.

mcqs.question: When should you prefer a SQL query over vector retrieval?
options: When the question maps to structured fields with exact values
When the corpus is PDF files
When the model has no tools
mcqs.explanation: Structured questions deserve queries; retrieval is for unstructured text semantics.

mcqs.question: What does grounding mean?
options: Anchoring model answers in verifiable sources so claims can be traced
mcqs.explanation: Grounded answers cite or rest on retrieved evidence, which is what makes evals measurable.

mcqs.question: What is re-ranking for?
options: Reordering retrieved candidates with a stronger model so the best chunks enter the prompt
mcqs.explanation: First-stage retrieval is cheap and approximate; re-ranking spends compute where it matters.

mcqs.question: Which metric best detects answers without support in the sources?
options: Groundedness or faithfulness against retrieved context
mcqs.explanation: Unsupported answers are the classic RAG failure; groundedness metrics target exactly that.

mcqs.question: Why must indexing pipelines be kept up to date?
options: Stale chunks make the model answer from outdated content
mcqs.explanation: Freshness is a pipeline property: re-embedding and re-chunking when sources change.

mcqs.question: What is the strongest reason to skip RAG for a small policy handbook that fits in context?
options: Putting the full handbook in the prompt is simpler and avoids retrieval failure modes
mcqs.explanation: When relevant content fits reliably in the window, retrieval is over-engineering.

mcqs.question: What does the question when NOT to use RAG actually test?
mcqs.explanation: Interviewers probe whether you can reason about alternatives and costs, per the field guide interview patterns.

scenarios.prompt: Users report that the documentation assistant cites the right document but the wrong sentence, and answers change when the same question is asked twice with slightly different wording.

code.code:
chunks = split_by_chars(doc, size=1500)
results = vector_store.search(embed(query), k=4)

scenarios.modelAnswer: Symptoms point to chunking and retrieval stability. Chunk by structure (headings, paragraphs) with overlap so facts are not cut mid-sentence, and make chunk metadata carry the document location for citations. Add hybrid search (keyword plus vector) and re-ranking so wording changes do not reorder good chunks away. Evaluate with a question set where the expected citation is known, and track retrieval metrics (recall at k) separately from answer quality so you know which layer fails.
rubric: Links wrong citations to chunking or retrieval, not generation
Proposes structure-aware chunking with overlap and citation metadata
Adds retrieval metrics on a labelled question set

scenarios.prompt: The legal team wants to ask questions about 40 structured contracts with amounts, dates and parties. They ask for a vector store over the exported PDFs.

code.code:
docs = [export_pdf(c) for c in contracts]
index = build_vector_index(docs)

scenarios.modelAnswer: Explain when not to use RAG: the questions are structured lookups (amounts, dates, parties), so parse the contracts into a relational or semantic layer and answer with queries or tool calls, with citations back to the clause. Keep the PDFs as evidence, not as the primary index. Vector retrieval is justified for unstructured questions such as how a clause is worded; for exact values a query is more reliable, auditable and cheap. A hybrid design can do both: query first, retrieval for narrative.
rubric: Identifies that structured questions favour queries over retrieval
Proposes extracting data into a queryable model
Keeps sources as evidence with citations
Allows retrieval for narrative or unstructured sub-questions

scenarios.prompt: A knowledge assistant answers well in demos but after a month cites policies that were replaced. The index is rebuilt manually every quarter.
scenarios.modelAnswer: Freshness is a pipeline property: rebuild incrementally when sources change (webhook or scheduler), record document versions in chunk metadata, and invalidate or re-embed changed documents. Add a staleness signal in answers (as-of date) and an eval that checks the assistant never cites a superseded policy. If sources have update timestamps, filter or sort by freshness at retrieval time and alert when drift exceeds a threshold.
rubric: Moves from manual periodic rebuilds to incremental updates
Versions documents and chunks for traceability
Adds staleness signals or freshness filtering
Adds an eval for superseded citations
